text_blocks.snippet: Ruth Bader Ginsburg was involved in several landmark Supreme Court cases, both as an advocate and as a Justice. As a lawyer, she argued six landmark cases on gender equality, notably _Frontiero v. Richardson (1973), which challenged gender-based discrimination in military benefits. As a Justice, she authored majority opinions in cases like _United States v. Virginia (1996), which ended VMI's male-only admissions policy, and _Olmstead v. L.C. (1999), which addressed the rights of people with disabilities. She also participated in cases like _Bush v. Gore (2000) and _Obergefell v. Hodges (2015).

list.title: Frontiero v. Richardson (1973):
list.snippet: Ginsburg argued that denying female military members the same benefits afforded to male members based on gender was unconstitutional.

list.title: Weinberger v. Wiesenfeld (1975):
list.snippet: Ginsburg successfully challenged a Social Security provision that treated widows and widowers differently.

list.title: Califano v. Goldfarb (1977):
list.snippet: This case involved a challenge to Social Security benefits that favored certain classes of widowers over others.

list.title: Duren v. Missouri (1979):
list.snippet: Ginsburg challenged the gender-based exemption for women from jury duty.

list.title: United States v. Virginia (1996):
list.snippet: Ginsburg wrote the majority opinion striking down the male-only admissions policy at the Virginia Military Institute.

list.title: Olmstead v. L.C. (1999):
list.snippet: The Court ruled that unjustified institutionalization of people with disabilities was a form of discrimination.

list.title: Friends of the Earth, Inc. v. Laidlaw Environmental Services, Inc. (2000):
list.snippet: Ginsburg wrote the majority opinion holding that residents near the North Tyger River had standing to sue Laidlaw for pollution that restricted their recreational use of the river.

list.title: Bush v. Gore (2000):
list.snippet: Ginsburg dissented from the ruling that effectively awarded the 2000 presidential election to George W. Bush.

list.title: Obergefell v. Hodges (2015):
list.snippet: Ginsburg joined the majority opinion that legalized same-sex marriage nationwide.

list.title: Whole Woman's Health v. Hellerstedt (2016):
list.snippet: Ginsburg was part of the majority that struck down Texas laws restricting access to abortion.

list.title: Timbs v. Indiana (2019):
list.snippet: Ginsburg wrote the opinion holding that the constitutional ban on excessive fines applies to state and local governments.
